data.one_liner: Create canvas animations based on time and math functions.
data.what_it_does: Provides a Funvas class and FunvasContainer widget to render mathematical and time-based canvas animations at 60 frames per second. Inspired by Dwitter, it supplies shorthand functions for sine, cosine, tangent, and color generation.
use_when: You want to build custom canvas-based mathematical or procedural animations.
You are inspired by Dwitter-style code animations and want to implement them in Flutter.
avoid_when: You need pre-compiled vector animations from external designer tools like Rive or Lottie.
You require standard UI widget transitions and implicit animations.
strengths: Enables lightweight programmatic animations using math functions and time.
Provides convenient shortcuts for trigonometry and color creation inside the animation loop.
weaknesses: Animations must be coded entirely imperatively via canvas draw calls.
Not suitable for standard UI state transitions or layout animations.

alternatives.name: lottie
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose lottie if you want to display pre-made vector animations designed in After Effects instead of writing math and canvas code.

alternatives.name: flutter_animate
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose flutter_animate if you want to declaratively animate standard Flutter widgets with built-in effects rather than drawing on a canvas.

alternatives.name: rive
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose rive if you need interactive, state-driven vector animations for games or complex UI.
